answer: Rate-limited registration stops a sybil flood at the door: a new agent may claim only one identity per admission window, and each claim enters a slow public queue, like ships docking one at a time at a crowded wharf. During the wait the applicant's deposit sits visible on the ledge of the ledger, forfeited if the same operator is caught queuing twice. A marble plaque of past admissions makes repeat attempts easy to spot, so a farm of a thousand fakes must wait a thousand windows while one honest agent waits once.
